programme.summary: The Claude Certification Program validates practitioners, architects and developers on real-world Claude solutions, not trivia.

certificationPage.summary: The CCAR-F certification focuses on informed tradeoffs implementing production-grade solutions with Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK, the Claude API and MCP.

references.summary: Claude Code permission modes vary in approval behavior; managed settings outrank local settings and auto mode may depend on availability. Enterprise deny rules cannot be weakened into human approval by a local mode or allow rule. Compare modes and human gates in actual workflows.
PreToolUse hooks can deny calls; exit code 2 blocks and communicates a reason. Do not confuse hooks with contextual instructions.

CLAUDE.md loads project instructions; path-scoped .claude/rules/*.md MARKDOWN files use YAML frontmatter with a paths field and load when matching files are read. A .yaml file in .claude/rules is NOT loaded as a rule. Instructions are not permission controls.

Subagents isolate context and inherit the parent conversation's permissions, usually with restricted tools. Restricting a subagent cannot grant a read or write prohibited by an inherited/managed deny. There is no documented magic directory-access grant via subagent creation; an authorized policy change or a genuinely already-permitted path is needed.

User-defined CLIENT tools run in your application's infrastructure: the model returns tool_use, your application executes the tool and sends tool_result. SERVER tools described here are Anthropic-provided and run on Anthropic infrastructure; a custom PII enrichment function does not become an Anthropic server tool merely by declaring it. Do not route restricted private processing onto a provider-hosted server tool if it must run on customer-controlled infrastructure.
The Claude Messages API can connect to remote HTTP MCP servers, with per-tool allowlists and deny rules; the connector does not directly run local STDIO MCP servers.
Structured outputs constrain JSON format, but some JSON Schema constraints such as minLength and maxLength require separate application-side validation.
Specific instructions, relevant diverse examples, and clear context improve Claude responses; avoid claiming an API behavior solely from prompting.
Place stable content before changing content; cache breakpoints cover exact prefixes. The default cache TTL is five minutes; one-hour TTL is explicit and has separate pricing.
Context includes system instructions, messages, tool definitions and responses; compaction addresses long-running interactions. A large window alone does not prevent context degradation.
Define measurable success criteria and evaluate realistic edge cases with task-specific grading; use the results to revise the Claude application rather than relying on definitions or impressions.
When evidence is insufficient, allow uncertainty, ground claims in source quotes and verify with citations instead of fabricating certainty.
Treat external tool results as untrusted input, enforce prompt-injection boundaries and least privilege, and test them; prompt text alone is not an authorization control.
Model capabilities and limits must be checked against the current Models API and per-model documentation; do not invent undocumented model behavior.

Claude Projects are focused workspaces with chats, project instructions and a knowledge base of uploaded files; the Claude Code CLAUDE.md mechanism is separate. Project details such as the project name are not automatically supplied as model context.

On paid Claude plans, a project approaching context limits can automatically enable RAG, retrieving relevant uploaded documents with a project knowledge search tool instead of placing everything in context.

The Claude Agent SDK loops through Claude decisions, tool execution and tool results until a final answer. Allowed and disallowed tools, approval modes and PreToolUse hooks are separate controls. A denied tool call prevents THAT call, but the agent may try another approach; denial does not automatically terminate the entire run or perform application rollback. Read-only tools may run concurrently; state-changing tools run sequentially. Overall Claude response latency cannot be guaranteed at a sub-second budget by tool timeouts alone.
